jobs.title: AI Sales Development Representative
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Hike Medical

Hike Medical is building the operating system for device-based care. We run the entire path that turns a prescription into a device on a patient's body — the back office that gets the patient ready, the point of care where they're evaluated, and the lab that makes the device. One company, built only for orthotics, prosthetics, and DME.

It's a $100B market, and more than half of every dollar never reaches a patient. It's lost to administration, denials, mispricing, and rework — while the person who needs the device waits. That gap is the business, and we built the machine that closes it, across three connected products:

  • Hike Intelligence — AI agents that run the revenue cycle, reading every faxed referral, verifying eligibility, chasing documents, and building audit-ready cases before a human touches a keyboard.

  • Hike Clinical — point-of-care software that lets a clinician evaluate a patient on any phone, generate a Medicare-compliant note, and order the device, all in a single visit.

  • Hike Lab — our own 3D-printing factory, turning a scan into a custom, PDAC-approved device shipped in days, not weeks.

Insoles are the wedge. DME is the bridge. Bionics is the destination. Read the full vision at bionics2040.com.

We've stealthily raised $22M through Seed and Series A, backed by top-tier investors who backed companies like OpenAI, Anduril, and Mercury early. We run a fast, results-first, high-ownership culture out of our new SF Rincon Hill office. If you want to work at the frontier of AI, manufacturing, and healthcare, this is the place.

The Opportunity

As an SDR, you are the engine of our provider growth. You'll prospect into Orthotic & Prosthetic (O&P) clinics, Podiatry practices, Physical Therapy centers, and independent DME providers across the country.

Your job is to get clinic owners and practitioners to take a demo of the Hike platform. Don't mistake these for small accounts—they're high-value providers running on analog workflows (fax intake, after-hours paperwork, denied claims, three-to-five-week lab turnarounds), which means large deals that move fast and enormous territory upside. You'll navigate front-desk gatekeepers with ease and speak credible clinical and business language to doctors, practice managers, and revenue leads.

You'll:

  • Run a high-velocity motion. Drive high-volume outreach (60–80 calls/day) to providers across the US. You know how to earn a receptionist's trust and get a decision-maker on the line.

  • Pitch practice economics, not products. You won't just talk about "insoles." You'll talk about denials, workflow efficiency, and profit margins — how Hike helps a provider see more patients in less time and stop bleeding revenue to rejected claims.

  • Qualify the real pain. Diagnose how a practice runs today: How do referrals arrive—still by fax? Where do they lose hours on intake and documentation? Who's their current lab? You're creating the wedge for our Account Executives.

  • Evangelize the platform. Many of these providers are old-school. You're the one showing them that AI-driven intake, born-compliant documentation, and PDAC-approved custom devices are real, reimbursable, and far better than the manual status quo.

What Excites Us

Selling to clinical executives and clinic owners takes a specific kind of polish and persistence. We're not filling a seat—we're looking for legends who can own this market. Specifically:

  • The strategic sales executive. 1–3 years of sales experience, ideally selling AI, software, or into medical practices, dental offices, independent pharmacies, or similar owner-operated businesses. You think like an owner and sell like a strategic partner, not a script-reader.

  • Poised and relentless. You don't flinch at the "the doctor is with a patient" objection. You navigate phone trees and front-desk staff with professionalism and persistence—and decision-makers take your call because you've earned it.

  • Coachable and curious. You can learn the difference between a pronated and a supinating foot, the basics of medical reimbursement, and how a denial actually happens—and you're hungry to.

  • High motor. This is a volume game. You're energetic, organized, and can manage a pipeline of hundreds of providers without letting a single lead slip through the cracks.

What You'll Own

  • Meeting setting. Booking 15+ qualified demos per month for our Account Executives.

  • Pipeline management. Managing a high volume of leads in HubSpot, with rigorous, disciplined follow-up.

  • Market feedback. Helping Marketing understand which messaging lands best with O&P professionals versus Podiatrists.

What You'll Get

  • Competitive compensation. Strong base ($60K–$90K) + uncapped commission ($100K–$150K OTE).

  • Meaningful equity. Real ownership in a high-growth startup backed by top VCs.

  • Accelerated growth. We reward A-players. Top performers get promoted fast—into closing roles and beyond—and are rewarded significantly for it.

  • Full benefits. Medical, dental, and vision coverage.

  • The hub. Daily collaboration with Hike's founding team out of our SF Rincon Hill office.

  • And yes—free custom insoles. Your feet will thank you.

jobs.title: Assistant Controller / Finance Manager
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Hike Medical

Hike Medical is a health tech company tackling musculoskeletal (MSK) health from the ground up—starting with the feet. We combine proprietary AI and deep-learning technology with clinical expertise to deliver custom 3D-printed insoles built from a simple at-home foot scan. In about five minutes, anyone can scan their feet from home, and our technology converts that scan into a custom orthotic that is 3D printed in Illinois and shipped directly to them. We partner with employers and health systems to make personalized foot care accessible, helping people move better and live pain-free.

As we scale, we are building out a finance function that can keep pace with rapid growth. This is a high-impact role for someone who wants ownership, visibility with leadership, and the chance to help shape the financial backbone of a mission-driven company.

The Role

We are looking for an Assistant Controller / Finance Manager to serve as the right hand to our finance lead and own day-to-day accounting operations. You will manage the close process, strengthen our controls and reporting, and partner across the business on budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis. This is a hands-on role with significant room to grow as the

company and finance team expand.

What You'll Do

  • Assist in the monthly, quarterly, and year-end close, including journal entries, account reconciliations, and accruals, ensuring accurate and timely results.

  • Prepare and review financial statements in accordance with U.S. GAAP and support management reporting packages for leadership and investors.

  • Manage core accounting operations including accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll support, and general ledger integrity.

  • Build, document, and improve internal controls, accounting policies, and scalable processes that support a growing business.

  • Support budgeting, forecasting, and variance analysis, partnering with department leaders to track spend and inform decisions.

  • Coordinate the annual audit and tax filings, serving as a key point of contact for external auditors and tax advisors.

  • Oversee cash management, including reconciliations, treasury reporting, and cash-flow forecasting.

  • Help select, implement, and optimize accounting and finance systems as we scale.

  • Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory, tax, and reporting requirements across jurisdictions.

What We're Looking For

  • 4–6 years of progressive accounting and finance experience, ideally combining public accounting and in-house/industry experience.

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field; CPA (or active candidacy) strongly preferred.

  • Strong working knowledge of U.S. GAAP and the full-cycle close process.

  • Experience owning or heavily contributing to month-end close, financial reporting, and

reconciliations.

  • Advanced Excel skills and hands-on experience with accounting/ERP systems (e.g., QuickBooks, NetSuite, or similar).

  • High attention to detail with strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.

  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to partner cross-functionally with non-finance stakeholders.

  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, high-growth environment and rolling up your sleeves.

Nice to Have

  • Experience at a startup, health-tech, manufacturing, or D2C/e-commerce company.

  • Exposure to inventory or cost accounting in a physical-product business.

  • Experience implementing or upgrading ERP and finance systems.

Compensation & Benefits

Salary range: $120,000 – $140,000 per year, plus equity.

Final compensation will depend on experience, qualifications, and overall fit. In addition to base

salary and equity, Hike Medical offers a comprehensive benefits package and the opportunity to make a meaningful impact at a fast-growing, mission-driven company.

How to Apply

If this sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you. Please submit your resume and a brief note about why you're excited about Hike Medical.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
This role is for candidates based in or open to relocating to San Francisco (Rincon Hill), in person 5 days a week. Full time. No remote opportunities are available.

About Hike Medical

Hike Medical is building the defining company in musculoskeletal care. We sit at the intersection of AI, robotics, and healthcare, across three product lines: a proprietary AI-vision platform that turns a 30 second web-based foot scan into custom 3D-printed orthotics; an AI agent platform that automates the entire DME workflow from pre-visit processing to claims and revenue cycle; and SoleForge, our vertically integrated 3D printing factory producing custom medical devices at a scale the industry has never seen.

Our customers are both the largest employers on earth and the biggest companies in orthotics and prosthetics. On the clinical side, we are live across the industry's largest national providers. On the employer side, Fortune 50 companies trust us to protect their on-their-feet workforces.

Custom insoles are just the wedge. Our long-term vision is bionics: AI-designed, robotically manufactured orthotic and prosthetic devices at scale, replacing a fragmented, manual industry that has not changed in decades. Insoles today, full DME tomorrow, bionics by 2040. Read the full vision at bionics2040.com.

We have raised $22M through Seed and Series A, backed by top-tier investors who invested early in companies like OpenAI, Anduril, and Mercury. We run a fast, results-first, high-ownership culture out of our SF Rincon Hill office. If you want to work on problems at the frontier of AI, manufacturing, and healthcare, this is the place.

The Role

As a Senior Software Engineer, you will build and ship the core systems behind Hike's AI healthcare platform. You will design scalable services, put AI into production, and deliver experiences that improve patient outcomes. From day one you will have real autonomy and clear impact.

We are deliberately open on the exact stack and on which area you join. We care more about how you think and what you ship than about any specific language, framework, or cloud. You will be placed on the team that best fits your strengths, on one of our three pods:

  • Hike Intelligence: AI agents that automate the back-office DME and revenue cycle workflow, from intake and eligibility to prior auth and billing.

  • Hike Clinical: the point-of-care and lab platform clinicians work in, from foot scan and evaluation to ordering custom devices.

  • Hike Lab and Marketplace: the manufacturing, automation, and commerce backbone behind SoleForge, plus the marketplace and admin tooling.

Why this is career-defining

  • Your code will help people move without pain.

  • You will have full autonomy to build, ship, and see the results, moving from idea to production in hours or days.

  • You will join a high-performing team of top engineers and AI researchers, where every hire makes a massive impact.

  • You will work in a culture where bureaucracy is not tolerated, fluff is frowned upon, and trust is the driving force.

What you will work on

  • Architect, build, and optimize scalable systems and services that power AI-driven healthcare workflows.

  • Take AI from prototype to reliable production.

  • Build the data pipelines, APIs, and integrations that connect our clinical, manufacturing, and back-office systems.

  • Ship user-facing experiences that move real metrics for patients and customers.

What we look for

  • A senior engineer with a track record of shipping production systems end to end.

  • Strong fundamentals across backend or full-stack, and comfort making architecture and infrastructure decisions.

  • Fluency with modern cloud and tooling. Experience putting AI into production is a plus, not a requirement.

  • Product-minded: you think about how your work affects real users.

  • A strong communicator who challenges assumptions and collaborates across engineering, AI, and product.

  • Driven to ship: you want control of your work from architecture to deployment, and you move fast.

  • Mission-focused: you are not here to optimize ad clicks, you want to build technology that changes lives.

What we ask

  • In person in our San Francisco Rincon Hill office, 5 days a week.

  • This is a hard job. Expect long hours and a high bar. In return the work is unusually rewarding, and you will see your impact quickly.

  • High ownership and low bureaucracy. Results come first.

  • We are a Series A company. You will help build the foundation, not maintain someone else's.

Hiring manager

Nik Varshney, CTO.

About Hike Medical

Hike Medical is building the operating system for device-based care. We run the entire path that turns a prescription into a device on a patient's body: the back office that gets the patient ready, the point of care where they're evaluated, and the lab that makes the device. One company, built only for orthotics, prosthetics, and DME.

It's a $100B market, and more than half of every dollar never reaches a patient. It's lost to administration, denials, mispricing, and rework while the person who needs the device waits. That gap is the business, and we built the machine that closes it, across three connected products:

  • Hike Intelligence: AI agents that run the revenue cycle, reading every faxed referral, verifying eligibility, chasing documents, and building audit-ready cases before a human touches a keyboard.

  • Hike Clinical: point-of-care software that lets a clinician evaluate a patient on any phone, generate a Medicare-compliant note, and order the device, all in a single visit.

  • Hike Lab: our own 3D-printing factory, turning a scan into a custom, PDAC-approved device shipped in days, not weeks.

Insoles are the wedge. DME is the bridge. Bionics is the destination. Read the full vision at bionics2040.com.

We've raised $22M through Seed and Series A, backed by top-tier investors who backed companies like OpenAI, Anduril, and Mercury early. We run a fast, results-first, high-ownership culture out of our new SF Rincon Hill office. If you want to work at the frontier of AI, manufacturing, and healthcare, this is the place.

The Opportunity

The GTM Associate is a junior Account Manager. You own the day-to-day relationship with a group of provider accounts, from the first onboarding call through activation and ongoing adoption of Hike's products. It is the entry point to the commercial side of Hike and a direct path to Account Manager, Account Executive, General Manager, or Operations leadership.

Our market is hard to sell into and hard to serve. O&P clinics, podiatry practices, physical therapy centers, and independent DME providers run on analog workflows: fax intake, after-hours paperwork, denied claims, three-to-five-week lab turnarounds. Succeeding here takes people who learn the industry deeply, speak credible clinical and business language, and stay close to customers until the product is working for them.

We hire sharp operators with 1 to 3 years of experience, often from banking, consulting, or a high-performing startup, who want to get into tech, AI, and healthcare and are willing to learn our market from the ground up. You will work alongside senior Account Managers, build real customer relationships early, and earn a larger book of accounts as you prove yourself.

What You'll Do

  • Onboard and activate new providers. Run onboarding calls, get clinicians and staff set up on the platform, and drive each account to its first orders and steady usage.

  • Manage a book of accounts. Be the main point of contact for your providers. Run regular check-ins, track account health, and spot clinicians who are stuck, ordering with errors, or going quiet.

  • Solve problems end to end. Handle the day-to-day issues that come up with orders, billing, and workflow, and work with our support, operations, and engineering teams to resolve them.

  • Support data quality and implementation. Work with our software engineers to get provider data set up correctly during onboarding, so Hike Intelligence can run the revenue cycle cleanly.

  • Grow accounts. Identify opportunities to bring more of Hike's products and more clinicians into an account, and hand qualified opportunities to the right teammate.

  • Keep clean records. Maintain disciplined follow-up and notes in HubSpot for every account you touch.

  • Share what you hear. Help Marketing and Product understand what lands with O&P professionals versus podiatrists, and where providers get stuck.

What Excites Us

  • Mission driven. Hike exists to provide high-quality access to care to the largest number of people possible. There are 7 billion humans on earth, and all of them should have custom orthotics.

  • The owner-operator mindset. You have 1 to 3 years of experience, ideally from banking, consulting, or a fast-moving startup. You think like an owner, not a script-reader, and you're drawn to hard problems in tech, AI, and healthcare.

  • Coachable and curious. You can learn the difference between a pronated and a supinating foot, the basics of medical reimbursement, and how a denial happens, and you want to. You pick up new domains fast.

  • Poised and relentless. You don't flinch at "the doctor is with a patient." You work through front-desk staff, phone trees, and messy workflows with professionalism and persistence.

  • High motor and organized. You move fast, keep your commitments, and manage a high volume of accounts without letting anything slip through the cracks.

What You'll Get

  • Competitive compensation. Strong base plus meaningful upside tied to account and team performance.

  • Meaningful equity. Real ownership in a high-growth startup backed by top VCs.

  • A clear path up. Top performers are promoted fast into Account Manager, AE, and other ownership roles, and are rewarded significantly for it.

  • Full benefits. Medical, dental, and vision coverage.

  • The hub. Daily collaboration with Hike's founding team out of our SF Rincon Hill office.

  • Free custom insoles. Your feet will thank you.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Hike Medical

Hike is building the operating system for device-based care. We make software and hardware for the $60B+ DMEPOS market: Hike Intelligence automates intake and revenue cycle with AI agents, Hike Clinical runs point of care, and SoleForge, our 65,000 sq ft facility in Peoria, IL, 3D prints custom medical devices at a scale few facilities in North America can match.

We raised $22M from investors including SAGA Ventures, founded by Max Altman. Our founder's family has worked in orthotics and prosthetics for three generations, and we know these workflows better than anyone in the world. We build for clinicians because we come from them.

The opportunity

Outbound already works at Hike. Cold outreach books meetings, meetings turn into pipeline, and pipeline turns into national partnerships. We proved the motion. Now we need someone to pour fuel on the fire.

That is the job. Take a working playbook, make it 10x bigger, and make it better while you scale it. This is not a zero-to-one role where you spend a year finding message-market fit. The message lands. The market is wide open. The clinics we sell to have never been sold to well, and we are early in a market with no default software vendor.

You will own top of funnel for the company. Not manage it. Own it. Every qualified meeting on an AE calendar traces back to your team, your campaigns, and your playbook. You report directly to leadership and carry a pipeline number.

This is a three-part job:

1. Build and lead the SDR team. Recruit, hire, ramp, and manage SDRs. Set quotas, run standups, coach calls, and hold the bar. You inherit reps who are already booking meetings. Your job is to grow the team into a machine.

2. Scale outbound as a system. Own targeting, sequencing, messaging, channel mix, and the tooling stack. Sharpen what works and add what's missing. Podiatry practices, O&P clinics, and DME providers do not respond to generic SaaS outreach. You will run campaigns that actually land with clinicians: direct mail with a 3D-printed insole in the box, event-driven plays around industry conferences, provider-to-provider referral loops, whatever works.

3. Sell. You carry your own book alongside the team. You prospect, cold call, and book meetings yourself. If you have not written a cold email in two years, this is not your job.

What you will do

  • Hire and manage a team of SDRs, scaling headcount as pipeline converts

  • Own the meetings-booked and qualified-pipeline number for the company

  • Take our proven sequences and campaigns and multiply their volume without losing quality

  • Design and run multi-channel campaigns across phone, email, LinkedIn, direct mail, and events

  • Harden the outbound playbook: ICP definition, messaging by persona, objection handling, sequences

  • Own the outbound tech stack and keep CRM data clean enough to trust

  • Report weekly on pipeline metrics with real numbers, not vibes

  • Partner with marketing on campaign creative and with AEs on handoff quality

  • Recruit continuously. Your bench is your job security.

What we need

  • 5+ years in B2B sales development, including 2+ years managing SDRs or BDRs

  • A track record you can show in numbers: quota attainment, meetings booked, pipeline sourced, reps promoted

  • You have scaled an outbound motion before, not just maintained one

  • Strong writer. Your sequences will be read by physicians and clinic owners.

  • Fluent in modern outbound tooling and comfortable putting AI to work on research, personalization, and ops

  • Healthcare, medtech, or DME experience is a plus, not a requirement. Hunger to learn the market is required.

  • In person in San Francisco

Why this role

  • A motion that already works. You scale a fire, you don't start one.

  • Direct line to the CEO and a seat in go-to-market strategy, not a middle-management layer

  • A product clinics actually want, backed by a manufacturing operation you can put in a prospect's hands

  • Clear path to VP-level scope as the team scales

  • Top-of-market comp: $140K-$170K base, $200K-$250K OTE, equity, full benefits

Own Hubspot / Salesforce end to end, wire the stack around it, design the processes that move a lead from a cold list to a closed partnership, and turn the data into a forecast leadership can bet on.

You are the admin, the architect, and the person who decides what "clean" means. If the org has drifted, you fix it. Where it's greenfield, you build it right the first time.

  2. Build the revenue stack and the data layer. CRM is the core, but it doesn't stand alone. Own the tooling around it — enrichment, sequencing, dialers, CPQ, BI, and the integrations that keep them in sync. Kill what doesn't earn its seat. Make sure every system writes back to one source of truth.

  • Build and administer the full revenue tech stack across sales, marketing, and CS

  • Instrument new motions as we launch them — new channels, new segments, new products

  • Fluent in modern revenue tooling and comfortable putting AI to work on ops, enrichment, and analysis

  • Healthcare, medtech, or DME experience is a plus, not a requirement. Hunger to learn the market is required

  • In person in San Francisco

  • Total ownership of the systems the whole company runs on

  • Clear path to a Head of / Director of RevOps scope as the org scales

About the Founding Head of Talent

Hiring is one of the most important things we do. We're looking for our first Head of Talent to build the function from the ground up. This is a company-building role, not an HR role. You'll work directly with founders to answer: What should we hire next? How do we attract exceptional people before everyone else? How do we maintain our talent bar while scaling? How do we build a recruiting engine that compounds?

You'll own recruiting end-to-end while helping shape org design, hiring philosophy, interview quality, and how we scale as a company.

What You'll Do

  • Own company-wide hiring across engineering, AI, product, GTM, operations, clinical, manufacturing, and leadership

Product Development Program Management

  • Own device programs from concept and requirements through Proto, EVT, DVT, PVT, launch, and sustaining

  • Turn clinical and biomechanical needs into product requirements and engineering specs, with traceability from user needs through design inputs, outputs, and verification

  • Run design reviews, design freeze, and phase-gate exit reviews with clear, measurable entry and exit criteria

  • Coordinate work across mechanical, clinical, software, and customer teams; own integrated schedules, dependencies, and the critical path

  • Drive system-level tradeoffs between clinical performance, comfort, durability, cost, and lead time, and document the decisions

  • Own product roadmap execution as Hike expands from insoles into braces, other DME devices, and eventually powered orthotic and prosthetic devices

  • Own BOM, engineering change orders and notices (ECO/ECN), and configuration control in PLM

  • BS in Mechanical, Biomedical, Materials, or Manufacturing Engineering, or a related field

  • You're resourceful, move quickly, and enjoy building systems from scratch

  • You don't need excessive process to produce great outcomes

  • You have experience at a high-growth startup, building processes and teams while shipping product

  • Background in soft goods, or wearables

  • Experience with mass customization or patient-specific devices

  • Experience with electromechanical or powered medical devices (sensors, actuators, batteries, IEC 60601)

  • Experience with FDA submissions (510(k) or exemption strategy) or reimbursement (HCPCS/DME) programs

  • Exposure to smart manufacturing: machine vision, manufacturing execution systems (MES), in-line data collection

Why Hike

  • Own the product and the factory that makes it, a scope few hardware roles offer

  • Direct access to leadership and visibility on company-defining programs

  • Build the hardware program function at an early-stage medical device company
